test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2021: Official Paper (Held On : 10 June 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I never could quite get the idea ________ my mind that I should do some teaching, yet

I felt a great deal of satisfaction with the pastorate.
solution:
The correct answer is "**out of**". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the first place, "**out of my mind**" is a phrase that means '**stop thinking** about (something)'.
 
• As we can see, the sentence is talking about an **idea** about which he/she could **not stop thinking**. Thus, the application of **'out of mind'** is **appropriate** for this sentence.
 
 
• Example: *Put that naughty thought out of your mind.*
 
• Example: *He took his glasses out of his bag.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, all other alternatives are incorrect except "**out of**".
 
• The complete sentence is:* I never could quite get the idea out of__ my mind that I should do some teaching, yet I felt a great deal of satisfaction with the pastorate.​*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Let us understand the implication of the remaining options:
 
• The word "**out act**" means to **outperform** other actors in a play, movie, or other performance by being a better actor than them.
 
 
• Example: *It's important for supporting actors to avoid outacting the superstars.*
 
 
 
• The word "**outcome**" denotes the **result** or effect of an action or an event.
 
 
• Example: *Your result is the outcome of your hard work.*
 
 
 
• The word "**outcast**" means a person who is **no longer accepted** by society or by a group of people.
 
 
• Example:* He was an outcast in high school.*
